headline: The Dutch government approved a national quantum strategy that aims for technological leadership by 2035 and sets deadlines for government bodies to move to encryption that quantum computers could not break.
score_reason: National policy with firm security deadlines, but it brings no new dedicated funding.
importance_line: Dutch government bodies and quantum start-ups get dated goals, but the strategy adds no new money and admits that the timing of a code-breaking quantum computer is uncertain.
summary: The Quantum Insider reports that the Dutch Cabinet has approved a government-wide quantum strategy aiming for technological leadership and less dependence on non-EU suppliers by 2035. It asks government bodies to finish moving high-risk systems to post-quantum cryptography, encryption designed to resist quantum computers, by the end of 2030, but the plan creates no new fully funded programme and says ambitions will be adjusted if money is short.
